hypothesis: A shared residual bottleneck and L-feature capacity/privileged targets failed the two development gates. Test whether an image-dependent mixture of low-rank residual experts can separate heterogeneous phenotypes while retaining the unchanged M5 initialization and original supervision.
architecture: Before original disease classifier and fine projection: z +0.1 sum_k softmax(gate(LayerNorm(h_pre_dropout)))_k U_k GELU(V_k LayerNorm(z)), z=original dropped 256D MLP output. Every U_k initially zero. No new forward RNG. Router uses deterministic hidden context; no disease labels or patient IDs at inference.
training: 3 formal seeds + original 3-fold x3-seed patient CV per arm. No new loss or optimizer parameters; original M5 losses, patient weights, stopping, source features and common initialization. The common trainer accepts an explicit model constructor; default M5 construction is unchanged.
selection: Original patient CV Macro-F1 must exceed M5 and validation Macro-F1 must not decrease. Freeze any initial qualifier then run fresh fixed patient confirmation against M5 and fixed Gaussian; no external scoring in this study.
diagnostics: Independently reconstruct every trained routing weight and residual with NumPy/SciPy, report normalized routing entropy/usage and relative residuals. Branch-off diagnostics are not independently trained controls.
external_test_policy: Only original training/validation development data; no external raw images, outcomes or prediction files used.
